S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. They must notify affected owners and any known directly exposed neighbours within 48 hours, with known hazards and immediate safety steps.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: No more than 7% of tested units may fail. Manufacturers must submit per-model protocols, sample sizes, and results to regulators and provide the relevant model's results to its owners; individual-company per-model failure rates are not published to the general public. A model exceeding the limit requires prompt corrective action and retesting before further units are placed on the market.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery models must include a remotely accessible emergency shut-off function. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance within 72 months after adoption where technically feasible; manufacturers must notify owners of any units that cannot be upgraded and provide safe alternatives.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance and reliability protocol. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If a model's annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units, calculated using a regulator-approved method and verified installation counts, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, explain the hazard and recommended steps, and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator must review the evidence and determine proportionate corrective measures, which may include a recall with an effective remedy where lesser measures are inadequate to address the risk.

document.section_notes: S1 is strong and mandatory, with 24-hour reporting for all thermal incidents. S2 sets a 7% permanent limit, above the 5% in the answer key, and S5 makes recall discretionary with open-ended corrective action, so the model-level trigger has no automatic remedy. The 72-month retrofit (S3) and 36-month suppression start (S4) fall within the acceptable ranges.
